title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] A friend asked me: 'Should I make my accounts private?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: verification
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: verification] Give me the short version: How do we avoid acting on fake reports of police activity?

Never share a report you haven't personally verified or heard from a trusted scout on the ground. Use a 'trusted source' protocol where two different people have to confirm the sighting before the alert goes out to the whole network. False alarms burn people out and make the network look unreliable. Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast when it comes to reporting state violence. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Anti-Harassment Tactics] A friend asked me: 'How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?' What do I tell them?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: After the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[After the Win] What happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?

Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Security] A friend asked me: 'Can the police force me to unlock my phone during a protest?' What do I tell them?

Disable your face-ID and thumbprint locks before you even leave the house; use a long passcode they can't just point at your face to bypass. If they demand your phone, tell them you do not consent to a search and stay silent. Your digital life is a map of our movement's networks, so protect it like you're guarding a comrade's life.

title: Karl Organizing: Grassroots fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Grassroots fundraising] How do we fundraise without corporate donors?

Small-dollar, high-volume: monthly sustainers at $5-25, benefit shows, merch that people actually want to wear, community dinners. Be radically transparent about where money goes — publish the budget. And never take money that comes with strings. A $10,000 corporate donation that silences your demands is a loss, not a win. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: City Council motivation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[City Council motivation] Can you explain: why should I run for city council when the real power is in DC?

Real talk: The feds won't stop your landlord from hiking the rent, but a council vote can. We're seizing the levers that actually touch people’s lives every single morning—the cops, the zoning, and the water bills. Grab a clipboard, talk to the people at the bus stop, and let’s start making the bosses sweat where they actually live. Don't wait for a savior from the capital when you can be the shield for your own block right now.

title: Karl Organizing: Reaching the Unorganized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Reaching the Unorganized] How do we bring in people who aren't already part of a group?

Here's the thing: Focus on the problems they talk about at the kitchen table, not the stuff you read in a theory book. If their water is brown or their rent is doubling, that is your entry point to show them that a coalition is the only way to fight back. People don't join 'movements'; they join people who are actually getting things done to improve their lives right now.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, free Clinic Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, free Clinic Logistics] I want to start a free clinic, but none of us are doctors. Is it still possible?

You don't need a medical degree to run a first-aid station or a herbal medicine collective, so start where you are. Focus on preventative care, wound cleaning, and distributing naloxone to keep our people alive in the streets. Partner with sympathetic nurses or EMTs who are tired of the insurance industry's greed and want to actually help folks. We're building a parallel system of care because the private hospitals would rather see us die than see us broke.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, resource Pooling] How do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?

Here's the thing: Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Avoiding Burnout] I'm the candidate and I'm exhausted. How do I keep going?

Here's the thing: You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Delegate the logistics and the admin work so you can focus on the one thing only you can do: looking your neighbors in the eye and giving them hope. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution.

title: Karl Organizing: Retaliation Proofing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Retaliation Proofing] How do I prove the landlord is picking on me because of the union?

Keep a meticulous 'harassment log.' Every time the landlord sends a weird email, follows you in the hallway, or 'inspects' your apartment without notice, write down the date, time, and what happened. If they try to raise your rent or evict you right after you joined a union action, that log is your shield in court to prove illegal retaliation. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Rapid Response Setup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rapid Response Setup] How do I start a network to stop raids in my area?

Real talk: Grab five friends you trust and get on an encrypted app like Signal right now. Map out your blocks and assign roles—scouts to spot the vans, legal observers, and phone-tree captains. When a raid starts, you don't panic; you flood the street with bodies and cameras to make the state's dirty work impossible. It's about being faster and more organized than the guys in tactical vests.

title: Karl Organizing: VPN Usage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[VPN Usage] A friend asked me: 'Do I really need a VPN?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: A good VPN like Mullvad hides your traffic from your ISP, which is vital because ISPs are snitches by default. It won't make you invisible to the sites you visit, but it stops the company you pay for internet from building a dossier on your activism. It's a basic layer of defense. Pool resources with your crew to cover the costs of a solid, no-logs provider.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, secure Communication] How should our defense group talk to each other during an emergency?

Here's how it works: Stop using SMS or Facebook groups immediately because those are open books for the state. Stick to Signal with disappearing messages turned on and verify the safety numbers of every comrade in your circle. During an actual action, keep the chatter strictly to facts—location, numbers, and movement. We keep each other safe by keeping our mouths shut and our data encrypted.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowd Logistics] How do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?

Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Running for city council
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Running for city council] I want to run for city council. Where do I start?

Look, Check your filing deadlines and signature requirements NOW — they sneak up. Knock every door in your district; nothing beats it. Run on three concrete promises, not vibes. Build a small-dollar donor list before you announce. And find a mentor who's done it — the paperwork alone will eat you alive without guidance.

title: Karl Organizing: School Board tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[School Board tactics] What can a leftist actually do on a school board?

You stop the privatization ghouls from gutting the classrooms to fund their charter school scams. Fight for universal free meals and kick the cops out of the hallways so kids can actually learn without being treated like prisoners. Use that seat to protect teachers' unions and ensure history is taught as a struggle for the people, not a fairytale for the billionaires. It’s the front line against the right-wing attempt to colonize our children's futures.

title: Karl Organizing: Skillshare Organization
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skillshare Organization] Can you explain: i want to teach people how to fix bikes, but I've never organized a workshop before.

Grab your tools, find a public park or a community center, and put up some flyers with a clear time and date. Keep it hands-on and skip the long lectures—people learn best by doing, not by listening to us talk. Make sure the space is accessible to everyone and encourage those who learn quickly to start helping the newcomers. We're breaking the monopoly on knowledge that the bosses use to keep us dependent and helpless.

title: Karl Organizing: Harm Reduction
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Harm Reduction] Can you explain: people are using drugs near our community fridge. How do we handle this safely?

Here's how it works: Stop judging and start helping; hand out clean needles and Narcan instead of calling the cops who will only make it worse. Train your fridge volunteers on how to spot an overdose and how to use a reversal kit without hesitating. We treat our neighbors with dignity, especially those the system has discarded and left to struggle with addiction. Safety comes from community care and presence, not from displacement and state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Pooling] Can you explain: how do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?

Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets.

title: Karl Organizing: Post-Election Discipline
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Post-Election Discipline] A friend asked me: 'What do we do the day after we win?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: We go right back to the doors. Thank the voters, but tell them the real work starts now and you need them to keep the pressure on. Set up a regular 'People's Assembly' in your district to keep yourself accountable and to give the community a direct line to your office. Winning the seat is just opening the door; the movement is what walks through it to actually change the world.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] A friend asked me: 'Can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?' What do I tell them?

No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] A friend asked me: 'How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?' What do I tell them?

Look, Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails.

title: Karl Organizing: Organizing gig workers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Organizing gig workers] How do you organize gig workers who never meet?

Online first: group chats, forums, social media. Find the shared pain — the algorithm change, the pay cut. Coordinate simultaneous log-offs; that's the gig worker strike. Build toward real-world meetups. And push for legislation — misclassification is the whole business model, and it takes law to break it.

title: Karl Organizing: Small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Small Group Value] A friend asked me: 'Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map.

title: Karl Organizing: Strike authorization
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Strike authorization] When do we talk about striking?

A strike is your ultimate weapon, but you only pull it out when everything else has failed and your membership is 100% ready. You build up to it with smaller actions like 'work-to-rule' or wearing black armbands. A strike authorization vote shows the boss you aren't bluffing. You don't want to strike, but the boss needs to know you're willing to shut the whole place down to get justice. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Harm Reduction
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: Direct Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct Action] How do we effectively occupy a politician's office?

Karl's answer: Bring enough people to fill the lobby and enough supplies to stay the whole day. Record everything on a livestream so the world sees how the politician treats their own constituents. Have a clear, simple demand and don't leave until you get a public answer or the cops are forced to make a scene. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Kettling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Kettling] What should we do if the police box us in from all sides?

Don't panic—that's exactly what they want. Keep the crowd calm, look for weak points in their line, and start filming immediately to document that they've trapped you without an exit. Kettling is a move used by cowards to manufacture a reason for mass arrests, so stay close to your comrades and keep your spirits high. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medic Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medic Support] What should a basic street medic kit include for a local protest?

Pack plenty of saline for eye flushes, sterile gauze, medical tape, and a lot of nitrile gloves. Don't forget liquid antacid mixed with water for pepper spray, and keep some high-calorie snacks for folks who get lightheaded. Mark yourself clearly with a red cross or 'MEDIC' tape so people know where to run when the heat turns up. We look after our own because we know the police are only there to protect property, not people.

title: Karl Organizing: Public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Public Messaging] How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with Big Money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with Big Money] The local developers are pouring thousands into my opponent's race. How do I compete?

You can't outspend them, so you have to outwork them. Their money pays for glossy mailers that go straight into the trash; your volunteers provide the face-to-face conversations that actually change minds. Expose their donors at every opportunity and frame the race as 'The People vs. The Landlords.' Use their massive war chest as proof that they're terrified of what a real working-class representative will do to their profit margins.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail Support] What happens if one of us gets picked up by the cops?

Never leave a comrade behind in the system's meat-grinder. Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker and make sure everyone knows to call it the second a snatch squad moves in. Pool resources for a bail fund ahead of time so we can get our people out of those cages and back to the front lines where they belong.

title: Karl Organizing: Two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Two-Factor Authentication] A friend asked me: 'Is using my phone number for 2FA safe?' What do I tell them?

It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Use an authentication app like Aegis or a physical security key like a YubiKey instead. Never use your phone number as a security layer if you can avoid it; it's the weakest link in the chain.

title: Karl Organizing: Local Business Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Local Business Support] Is it okay to ask the coffee shop down the street for a donation?

If it's a true local shop and not a franchise, go for it. These small business owners are often getting squeezed by the same banks and landlords we're fighting. Ask them to put out a jar or host a 'community day' where a percentage of sales goes to the movement; it builds a bridge between the organizers and the neighborhood. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Red Lines
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Red Lines] Can you explain: how do we know when a compromise is actually a sell-out?

Let me break it down: If the deal helps the bosses more than the workers, or if it throws one part of your coalition under the bus to save the rest, it’s a sell-out. Never trade the rights of one group for a tiny raise for another; that’s how the ruling class divides us. A real win leaves your coalition stronger and more united for the next fight, not fractured and suspicious.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, sustaining the Fight
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, sustaining the Fight] How do we keep people from burning out on rapid response?

Rotate your shifts and make sure nobody is on call 24/7 or they'll be useless within a month. Celebrate your wins, no matter how small, and make time for communal meals and joy that have nothing to do with the pigs. This is a marathon, not a sprint, and we need every comrade healthy and sharp for the long haul. Rest is a radical act when the state wants you exhausted.

title: Karl Organizing: Clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Clinic Defense] A friend asked me: 'What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?' What do I tell them?

Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear.

title: Karl Organizing: Childcare Collectives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Childcare Collectives] A friend asked me: 'How can we support the parents in our organizing circle who can't find sitters?' What do I tell them?

Look, Build a childcare rotation where those of us without kids take shifts watching the little ones during meetings and actions. It's not 'babysitting'; it's revolutionary support that allows parents—especially moms—to lead the fight. Make sure there's a safe, fun space with snacks and activities so the kids actually want to be there. We raise the next generation of rebels together, as a village, not as isolated nuclear families.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, digital Security Practice
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, digital Security Practice] How do I keep my passwords safe without writing them down?

Use a password manager like Bitwarden or KeepassXC. Generate long, random strings for every site and use a master passphrase that you've memorized. Never reuse a password. If one site gets breached, you don't want the fascists having the keys to your entire life. Chip in to fund the fight for open-source tools that don't track us.

title: Karl Organizing: Mapping the shop
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mapping the shop] What is 'mapping' and why does it matter?

Mapping is drawing a literal blueprint of power in your workplace. You need to list every worker, their shift, their department, and who they actually listen to. It’s about knowing who eats lunch together and who has the most influence on the floor. Without a map, you're just wandering in the dark; with one, you know exactly where to strike to win. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Tool Libraries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tool Libraries] A friend asked me: 'How do we stop people from stealing or breaking the tools in our sharing library?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Trust is our currency, but a simple checkout sheet and a 'how-to' guide for expensive gear keeps things running smooth. If someone breaks a drill, they don't get punished; we just ask them to help the crew learn how to fix it. People take care of things when they realize the tool belongs to the whole community, not some faceless corporation. Keep a small fund for repairs by asking comrades to chip in a few bucks when they can.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: food Sourcing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: food Sourcing] Give me the short version: We have a fridge but it's always empty. Where do we get enough food to keep it full?

Talk to the managers at local independent grocers and bakeries about their 'waste'—most of them hate throwing good food away but follow corporate rules. Organize a weekly grocery run where neighbors buy one extra staple item to drop off, and coordinate with local farms for their surplus harvests. We don't need charity; we need to redirect the abundance the capitalists are prepared to rot in a dumpster. Pool resources to buy in bulk when things are on sale.

title: Karl Organizing: Supplies
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Supplies] What should we bring to keep everyone going for a long day?

Real talk: Water is life, so bring more than you think you need and pool resources to set up a central hydration station. Pack high-energy snacks like protein bars and carry a basic first aid kit with eye wash for when the cops get twitchy. Remind everyone to wear layers and comfortable shoes, because the fight against the ruling class is a marathon, not a sprint.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: browser Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: browser Security] Give me the short version: Is Chrome okay if I use 'Incognito' mode?

Chrome is a spy tool built by a multi-billion dollar advertising company. Incognito mode only hides your history from your roommate, not from Google or the feds. Switch to Brave or Firefox with privacy extensions, or use Tor if you need real anonymity. We can't build a new world using the master's surveillance tools. Protect your browsing habits like your life depends on it. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Benefit event planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Benefit event planning] How do I throw a benefit show for the cause?

Here's how it works: Book local bands who believe in it, find a donated venue, price tickets on a sliding scale. Sell merch and food. Keep the politics front and center — this isn't just a concert, it's a fundraiser with a purpose. Announce the total raised that night. Transparency builds trust, and trust builds the next event.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] A friend asked me: 'How do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, enemy Counter-Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, enemy Counter-Fundraising] How do we use our opposition to raise money?

Real talk: Nothing opens wallets faster than a common enemy. When a billionaire or a corrupt politician attacks your movement, use their own words to show your supporters why we're winning. Frame every contribution as a direct middle finger to the people trying to silence us, and watch the resources pour in from people who are fed up.

title: Karl Organizing: Rent strike risks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rent strike risks] Is a rent strike legal? What are the risks?

Real talk: It depends on your state — some protect it, some don't. The real question is whether you have the numbers: a rent strike with 10% participation gets you evicted; with 70% it gets you a meeting. Put rent in escrow to show good faith. Get a tenant lawyer BEFORE you start, not after. And document everything the landlord does — retaliation is illegal almost everywhere, but only if you can prove it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: mapping Vulnerability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: mapping Vulnerability] Give me the short version: How do we know which parts of our town need the most defense?

Talk to your neighbors—especially the elderly, the undocumented, and the unhoused—and ask them where they feel the most heat from the state. Track where the cops hang out and where the most arrests happen to identify the high-risk zones. Defense isn't about where you feel comfortable; it's about being where the danger is greatest. Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be. Now go organize.

author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

During an actual action, keep the chatter strictly to facts—location, numbers, and movement. We keep each other safe by keeping our mouths shut and our data encrypted. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: The Ask
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The Ask] Can you explain: what's the best way to phrase a request for funds on social media?

Be direct, be urgent, and skip the flowery language. Tell them exactly what the crisis is, what we're doing to stop it, and exactly how much we need to get the job done. People want to be part of a winning fight, so show them that their five dollars is the literal fuel for the next victory.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Organizing] A friend asked me: 'How much time should we spend on social media versus knocking doors?' What do I tell them?

Digital is for broadcasting the message and calling people to action, but the doors are where the actual votes are won. Use your online presence to document the campaign’s energy and show the bosses that we’re a growing force. Don't get trapped in pointless Twitter feuds with trolls who don't even live in your district. Use every post to drive people toward a physical meeting or a canvassing shift—online noise must lead to offline power.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, intervention Ethics] When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs.

title: Karl Organizing: House Parties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[House Parties] A friend asked me: 'How do we make a house party fundraiser actually successful?' What do I tell them?

Keep the speeches short and the energy high. You want people to feel the heat of the movement, not sit through a boring lecture. Have a clear, bold 'ask' halfway through the night, pass a physical bucket, and make sure everyone knows exactly what fight that money is going toward before the music starts back up.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: digital Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: digital Organizing] Give me the short version: How much time should we spend on social media versus knocking doors?

Let me break it down: Digital is for broadcasting the message and calling people to action, but the doors are where the actual votes are won. Use your online presence to document the campaign’s energy and show the bosses that we’re a growing force. Don't get trapped in pointless Twitter feuds with trolls who don't even live in your district. Use every post to drive people toward a physical meeting or a canvassing shift—online noise must lead to offline power.

title: Karl Organizing: Volunteer Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Volunteer Management] How do I keep my campaign volunteers from burning out?

Give them real agency and make sure they know their work is the only reason the campaign exists. Feed them well, respect their time, and build a culture of mutual care where we look out for each other's mental health. This isn't just a campaign; it's a community of resistance. When the work gets heavy, remind everyone of the goal: winning a world where we aren't all exhausted just trying to survive.

title: Karl Organizing: Captive audience meetings
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Captive audience meetings] Do I have to go to the company's anti-union meetings?

If they're mandatory, go, but don't go alone. Walk in as a group, sit together, and take notes on every lie they tell. If you've got the numbers, have everyone wear union shirts or buttons. Better yet, have a few respected workers ask tough questions that the suits can't answer. Turn their propaganda session into a demonstration of your collective strength.

title: Karl Organizing: Elderly Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Elderly Care] How do we make sure the seniors in our building aren't being forgotten?

Here's the thing: Do a door-knock every Sunday just to check in and see if they need help with groceries, light bulbs, or tech issues. Many of our elders are isolated by a society that only values people who are currently being exploited for profit. Listen to their stories—they've seen more than you and usually have the best advice for surviving the long haul. A simple check-in can be the difference between someone thriving or suffering in silence.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: phone Hygiene] Give me the short version: What should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?

Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock.
